passage:
"Boing!" said Sangeeta, squeezing the squeaky duck.
Gopika burst into laughter. "Again!"
"Boing!"
Gopika laughed and clapped. Then Sangeeta picked up her phone. Gopika looked at her, screwed up her face and said, "Waaa." She peeked between her fingers.
"Are you sad?" said Sangeeta.
"Waaa."
"You want me to look at you. I'm here." Gopika grinned and reached for the duck.

qa.q: What did Sangeeta squeeze to make Gopika laugh?
qa.a: She squeezed a squeaky duck.

qa.q: What does Gopika's peeking through her fingers suggest, and what else could it mean?
qa.a: It suggests the crying was a deliberate way to get Sangeeta's attention. She might also have felt a small bit of real sadness at being ignored.

qa.q: What could Sangeeta do that meets the need underneath?
qa.a: She can give a short bit of warm attention, then invite Gopika back to play, without making a fuss about the fake cry. 🙂

qa.q: How does Gopika see Sangeeta's phone?
qa.a: She probably sees it as taking Sangeeta's attention away, which is why she made the sound.

grounding: A toddler laughs spontaneously, then fake-cries to get attention, showing growing social understanding.

passage: Note from Tarun, nursery teacher. Anand, two and a half, laughed out loud when the door squeaked, a real belly laugh. A while later, when I turned to help another child, Anand dropped to the floor with a loud "Waaa" and peeked to see if I was looking. There were no tears. I went over and said, "You want me near you." He got up and took my hand. I will give him small moments of attention before he asks.

qa.q: What made Anand laugh out loud?
qa.a: The squeak of the door made him laugh.

qa.q: What does Anand's peeking to see if Tarun looked suggest, and what else could it mean?
qa.a: It suggests the cry was on purpose, to bring Tarun over. It might also mean he wanted comfort and used the way that had worked before.

qa.q: What could Tarun do next?
qa.a: Tarun can give small moments of warm attention ahead of time so Anand does not need the loud call.

qa.q: How might the other child have felt when Tarun turned away?
qa.a: They may have wanted Tarun's attention too, and they are also learning that adults share it.

grounding: A toddler laughs spontaneously and then fake-cries for attention, and caregivers respond to the need underneath.

passage:
The goat sneezed in the village yard, and Suraj burst out laughing, a real belly laugh.
Later, when his sister Ishita turned to chat with a neighbour, Suraj started to cry loudly, "Waaah!" But there were no tears, and he peeked between his fingers to see if she was looking.
Ishita didn't scold. She knelt beside him. "You want me to play with you?" Suraj nodded, and the crying stopped.

qa.q: What made Suraj laugh?
qa.a: The goat sneezed.

qa.q: What was Suraj feeling when he fake-cried?
qa.a: He felt left out and wanted his sister's attention, so he used a deliberate cry to get it.

qa.q: Which of Ishita's choices worked, and why?
qa.a: Responding to the need, asking if he wanted to play, worked, because it met his wish for attention without shaming him.

qa.q: How might the neighbour see Suraj's crying?
qa.a: The neighbour might find it funny, noticing the peeking and no tears.

grounding: A toddler laughs spontaneously and later fake-cries for attention, and his sister responds to the need underneath.

passage:
In their Copenhagen kitchen, Soo-ah was on a long phone call. Anders, on the floor, started to make crying noises. "Wah, wah." No tears. He watched her the whole time.
Soo-ah said goodbye and hung up. She sat beside him. "You wanted me. I'm here now."
Anders grinned and handed her a block. Earlier, when the cat had sneezed, his laugh had been real and sudden. This one was different, planned. But the need was real too.

qa.q: What did Anders hand Soo-ah?
qa.a: A block.

qa.q: What was Anders feeling when he made crying noises with no tears?
qa.a: He felt ignored during the long call and wanted his mother's attention.

qa.q: What did Soo-ah do that was wise?
qa.a: She responded to the real need for attention rather than scolding the fake cry.

qa.q: How might Soo-ah see the fake cry?
qa.a: She sees it as a sign that Anders is learning to use a display on purpose, and that he needs her.

grounding: A mother notices her toddler's fake cry is deliberate and responds to his need for attention.

passage: I'm Yamini, Deepika's aunt. When the family gathered to see the new baby cousin, Deepika sat quiet for a while. Then she started to cry, loud, but with no tears, peeking at us all through her fingers. Earlier she'd laughed properly at the baby's hiccups. Her mother didn't tell her off. She lifted Deepika onto her lap and said, "You want a cuddle too." Deepika snuggled in and stopped at once.

qa.q: What had Deepika laughed at earlier?
qa.a: The baby's hiccups.

qa.q: What might Deepika have been feeling when she fake-cried?
qa.a: She was probably feeling left out while everyone looked at the new baby and wanted attention too.

qa.q: What did Deepika's mother do that met the real need?
qa.a: She lifted her onto her lap and named her wish for a cuddle, without scolding.

qa.q: How does Yamini see Deepika's crying?
qa.a: Yamini notices the cry is put on but also sees the real feeling underneath.

grounding: An aunt sees a toddler fake-cry for attention when a new baby arrives, and her mother responds to the need.

passage:
Week one: the pressure cooker whistled and Suraj burst into a belly laugh, head thrown back. Salma laughed too.

Week three: Salma was on a long phone call. Suraj squeezed his eyes shut and wailed, but no tears came. Between wails he peeked to see if she was watching.

Salma ended the call and sat on the floor. "You want me, don't you?" He climbed into her lap, quiet at once.

Next morning she played with him before her calls, and he fetched his book.

qa.q: What made Suraj laugh in week one?
qa.a: The pressure cooker whistled.

qa.q: Why did Suraj peek between his wails?
qa.a: He was most likely feeling lonely and left out while Salma talked, and was checking whether his crying got her attention. Another reading is that he was simply bored during the long call.

qa.q: How could a parent respond to a fake cry like Suraj's?
qa.a: Like Salma, a parent can look at the need underneath, which here was attention, and meet it calmly, even planning time together before calls.

qa.q: How does Salma see Suraj's tearless wail?
qa.a: She sees it as a sign that he wants her, not as naughtiness, so she answers with closeness rather than scolding.

grounding: It shows a toddler moving from a spontaneous laugh to a deliberate fake cry, and a parent responding to the need underneath.
